label: Senate majority leader
title: Schumer support meter
subtitle: Senate Democratic caucus

groups.label: Expected to vote in the leadership election

context: Silence scores 0, so the many senators with no statement pull both averages toward the middle. The weighted figure sits closer to zero because nearly all firm opposition comes from incoming senators with the lowest weight. The caucus picks its leader by secret ballot, expected in early December.
method: Scale: +5 repeated vocal advocacy; +4 explicit endorsement with a stated reason; +3 says they will support him; +2 defends his record or leadership; +1 mild positive signal; 0 no statement found; -1 declines to commit when asked; -2 calls for new leadership or a leadership debate without ruling him out; -3 withholds support and sets conditions; -4 says it is time for new leadership, backs someone else or says their vote is currently no; -5 flatly says they will not support him.
Scores are one reader's judgment of public statements reported in the press. They are not vote predictions.
Weight = 1 + 9 x (years in Congress, House plus Senate, as of January 2027) / 50. The longest-serving member gets 10 and a brand-new senator gets 1.
Schumer himself is left out. Mary Peltola (Alaska) and Scott Colom (Mississippi) are left out while their races are uncalled.

The four retiring senators and Governor-elect Klobuchar are current senators, so they are in the main figure, but they are not expected to vote in the leadership election. The group table shows the figure without them.
A score of 0 means nothing was found on the record, not that the member is neutral. Many are allies who have simply not been quoted.
